import pandas as pd

def main():
    # Define source file paths
    source_files = [
        "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_66/test_0.csv",
        "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_66/test_1.csv",
        "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_66/test_2.csv",
        "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_66/test_3.csv",
        "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_66/test_4.csv"
    ]

    # List to hold dataframes
    dfs = []

    # Load each source CSV into a dataframe
    for file_path in source_files:
        df = pd.read_csv(file_path, dtype=str)  # Read all columns as string to match target schema
        # Ensure columns are exactly as target schema and in correct order
        df = df[['Year', 'Category', 'Nominee', 'Movie', 'Winner']]
        dfs.append(df)

    # Concatenate all source dataframes vertically (union)
    combined_df = pd.concat(dfs, ignore_index=True)

    # The target schema is ['Year', 'Category', 'Nominee', 'Movie', 'Winner'] all strings
    # Confirm all columns are string type
    combined_df = combined_df.astype({
        'Year': str,
        'Category': str,
        'Nominee': str,
        'Movie': str,
        'Winner': str
    })

    # There is no transformation needed on the data values themselves as source schema matches target schema
    # Just ensure no duplicates (optional, but usually good practice)
    combined_df.drop_duplicates(inplace=True)

    # Write the combined dataframe to the target CSV path
    target_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_66/target_multisource_cot.csv"
    combined_df.to_csv(target_path, index=False)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
